playbook: The game ends at 10:00 and is decided by kills minus losses in credits; a 0-0 draw is replayed, not lost.
Attacking into defenses (tesla coils, flame towers, pillboxes, turrets) loses: every unit that dies costs its full price.
Against a passive opponent: lose nothing and kill what comes; one kill with no losses wins.
A rusher attacks our base at 3:00-4:10 with about 20 infantry, then sends more waves; beat it with a defense and 10 infantry at home.
A big army committed all at once breaks an army; units sent in small groups die one by one.
When the score is even, keep defending: most opponents attack sooner or later and lose units to our defense, and a 0-0 draw is not a loss.

Attack only when clearly behind on score (by 500 credits or more) with a big army (25 or more units), late in the game, at a part of the enemy base where no defenses stand. Being behind by a few hundred credits is not a reason to attack.
When ahead on score, never attack: defend the lead.
An attack that is losing more than it kills, or that runs into defenses, must fall back at once.
Against a turtle (a base full of defenses, mines or aircraft) attacking almost always loses, even when slightly behind: keep defending.
Rocket infantry are the answer to aircraft and tanks; rifle infantry cannot hit aircraft.
Never attack into a fortified base (4 or more known defenses); fall back if the army is heading into one.

posture.defend: Stay at home and kill whatever comes. Right when ahead or even on score, early in the game, against a rusher or an aggressive opponent, or when the army is small
posture.gather: Build one big group at the staging point outside our base without attacking. Right when behind on score but the army is not big enough yet to attack
posture.commit: Attack with everything at once where no defenses stand. Right only when clearly behind on score (by 500 credits or more) late in the game with a big army, or against a passive opponent; never into a fortified base
posture.retreat: Pull the army back home now. Right when our army out of the base is losing more than it kills, is under fire from enemy defenses, or is heading into a fortified base

opponent.rusher: Attacks our base early (before about 4:30) with a big wave of infantry, and keeps sending waves
opponent.turtle: Builds many defenses (pillboxes, turrets, tesla coils, flame towers, mines), maybe aircraft; rarely attacks; a fortified base
opponent.fortified: Fortifies its ore field, keeps a big reaction army of infantry at home, attacks rarely and late
opponent.aggressive: Sends attack waves at our base again and again through the middle of the game
opponent.passive: Has no army and no defenses at all: we have seen its base and nothing there fights
opponent.unknown: Too early or too little seen to tell
